profile.campus: AWS Mississippi -- Madison County campus (Ridgeland/Canton industrial parks)
profile.address: Highland Colony Parkway, New Hope Grove, Ridgeland, Madison County, Mississippi, 39157
profile.reading:
This building is one of the data center structures Amazon Web Services is developing in Madison County, Mississippi, across two industrial park sites near Ridgeland and Canton, north of Jackson. The Mississippi Development Authority announced the project on January 25, 2024, describing it as a $10 billion private sector investment, the single largest capital investment in Mississippi history and about four times the size of the state's previous largest economic development project, expected to create at least 1,000 high-paying technology jobs. Governor Tate Reeves and the Development Authority did not name the investor at the time of the initial announcement; DataCenterDynamics and other trade press subsequently confirmed Amazon Web Services as the company behind the project.

Local Madison County press, including the Northside Sun and Canton-area coverage, and construction industry publications reported that multiple regional contractors were engaged to build what was described as twin AWS data centers on the two industrial park sites. Later state and company references cited investment figures beyond the original $10 billion as the project moved through additional phases; those later, larger figures were not independently confirmed against an AWS-owned or state-owned source for this page and should be read as a sequence of expanding announcements rather than one settled total.

AWS has not published a street address, opening date, floor area, or IT power rating for this individual building, and no source found for this page breaks the Madison County campus down building by building. This structure is treated as part of the documented AWS Mississippi footprint described above. Mississippi state officials, including Governor Reeves, framed the project publicly as a turning point intended to diversify the state economy beyond its traditional manufacturing and agriculture base, and Madison County has since seen a series of related road, water, and utility infrastructure discussions at the county and state level tied directly to the AWS buildout.

profile.capacity_note: Not published by AWS, the State of Mississippi, or Madison County at the building level. The Mississippi Development Authority disclosed a $10 billion total project investment and a 1,000 job target for the two-site campus as a whole at announcement; it did not publish per-building capacity, square footage, or opening dates, and this page does not infer them.
profile.facility_note: AWS has not identified this specific building by name, construction date, or function in any source found for this page. Local press described the project as twin data centers across two industrial park sites in Madison County; which site or building this entry corresponds to is not independently confirmed beyond its mapped coordinates.
profile.research_note: Reading written 2026-09-03 by srj-thinpage-writer session (Sonnet). Verified via fresh web search/fetch this session (not reused from 2026-09-02 batch without re-checking): AWS aboutamazon.com investment pages, state/city economic development releases, and named trade/local press, listed in sources. AWS does not publish a per-building street address, opening date, square footage, or IT power rating for this structure; none of the sources checked break the named campus down building by building. Prior batch's disclosure_policy claim (citing aws.amazon.com/about-aws/global-infrastructure/regions_az/ as directly confirming a non-disclosure policy) was checked directly this session and found to be overstated -- that page does not discuss facility-level disclosure at all -- so it was not reused verbatim; the non-disclosure finding here rests instead on the absence of building-level figures across every source checked, consistent with trade-press characterization of AWS's practice.
profile.regional_context: Madison County, Mississippi had no established hyperscale data center presence before AWS's January 2024 announcement, making the project a first-of-its-kind for the state rather than an addition to an existing cluster of the kind found in Virginia, Ohio, or Oregon. Power for the site is supplied in the Entergy Mississippi service territory. The Mississippi Development Authority's incentive package for the project was structured through the state's economic development statutes covering large scale private investment and required legislative action to finalize incentive terms, according to Mississippi Development Authority and state coverage. The project's scale relative to the state's prior economic development history, and its water and power demands in a market without existing large data center infrastructure, have been recurring subjects of Mississippi press coverage since the announcement.

reading.body:
This facility is one of several buildings within Amazon Web Services' newly established data center campus in Madison County, Mississippi, announced January 25, 2024 as a $10 billion initial commitment and described by Governor Tate Reeves as the largest capital investment in Mississippi history at that time. AWS has stated the campus will create at least 1,000 high-paying technology jobs and will consist of a minimum of three isolated, physically separate Availability Zones with independent power, cooling, and physical security, though the company does not publish individual building addresses, square footage, or per-facility power specifications as a stated security and operational policy. Subsequent state and local coverage cited escalating investment figures including $11 billion, $12 billion, and a cumulative $25 billion across Mississippi, though these were not independently cross-checked against AWS-owned sources and represent a sequence of expanding public commitments rather than a single fixed total.

AWS does not publish critical IT megawattage, cooling capacity, or construction timelines at individual facility level, so the power consumption and rack density of this specific building cannot be independently confirmed from operator disclosures. Mississippi has four mapped data center facilities across the state with no published megawatt figures from operator spec pages, placing this campus first by published capacity only because no other facilities in the state have disclosed specifications to this site. The state currently reports zero published megawatts of data center capacity, meaning AWS's actual power draw in Madison County remains undisclosed.

This campus remains in active buildout phase as of this research. Without published power specifications, the facility's contribution to AI scaling, its constraint on the regional grid, and its rank among US data center campuses by compute density cannot be assessed from disclosed facts. The investment scale and workforce commitment signal material capital commitment to the state, but measurable impact on AI infrastructure depends on capacity figures AWS has not released.
